/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 05 August 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 3063 (127)
Baltic Capesize Index: 5094 (316)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2236 (49)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1612 (-1)
Baltic Handysize Index: 879 (-2)
CAPESIZE
Another positive day for the market saw the upward trajectory continue, with gains recorded across both basins as sentiment remained firmly in owners’ favour. The BCI 182 5TC index advanced by a further $2,867 to settle at $46,201. The Pacific led the charge once again, with the C5 index climbing $1.050 to $16.295, while the C3 index also extended its recent rally, rising $0.560 to $36.070. In the Pacific, market conditions continued to firm on the back of healthy cargo volumes. Although only two C5 miners were active today, participants remained focused on the potential disruption from Typhoon Dolphin as it continues its approach towards China, with expectations that weather-related delays could further tighten prompt tonnage availability. Trading reflected the strengthening market. On C5, bids started the day around $15.50 against offers reported in the $16.50 region before improving steadily throughout the session. By the close, bids had reached $16.00, with reports of one major miner fixing at $16.30. In the Atlantic, momentum also remained firmly positive. South Atlantic and West Africa business continued to strengthen, with early September C3 bids heard in the low $35s, while a premium was being paid for 10-20 September laycans, culminating in reports of $36.10 concluded. Conditions out of West Africa also continued to improve. The North Atlantic added further support, with a handful of stronger trans-Atlantic fixtures indicating firmer underlying sentiment.
PANAMAX
An active day was recorded across both basins, with multiple fixtures reported across the routes and overall sentiment remaining positive. The P5TC continued its upward trajectory, gaining a further $442 to close at $20,128. In the Atlantic market participants have reported an increase in demand from the North, prompting Owners to raise offers, with bids following suit particularly for prompt tonnage. Fronthaul activity is also showing signs of improvement, with brokers noting that tonnage availability remains tight in the near term. Demand continues to outpace supply, supporting stronger fundamentals and reinforcing the positive market sentiment. The Pacific also maintained its constructive tone despite brokers continuing to describe the tonnage list as lengthy. Demand from both the North Pacific and Australia is helping absorb available capacity, while improving conditions in the Atlantic are drawing tonnage away from the Far East and contributing to a more balanced supply picture. Owners are reportedly holding firm on their rate expectations, with some seeking higher levels, helping to underpin the market's upward momentum.
Market sources have also highlighted that anticipated weather-related disruptions are encouraging Charterers to secure cover earlier than usual. Indonesia has likewise seen fixing levels improve, supported by fresh enquiry and increased competition for longer Pacific voyages, further strengthening sentiment across the basin. Period activity was also evident, with the Alexandra (81,870 2017) open Incheon on 11 August placed on subjects for 11-13 months, while the Xin Qi Meng (81,558 2021) open Zhoushan on the same dates was placed on subjects for the same duration at $19,000 with Swissmarine. The Perseus (81,210 2015) was fixed from Dalian for period business with Costamare. The scrubber fitted Haris II (82,190 2026) open Hong Kong 12/14 August was reported to have been placed on subjects for two laden legs, basis redelivery Singapore-Japan, at $22,000. Similarly, the Denita Wave (93,201 2011) open Kaohsiung on 5 August was fixed for the same period with Sinmal, although the rate remains undisclosed. The scrubber fitted Canopus (80,992 2021) open Singapore 7/8 August was reported to have fixed for 6-8 months redelivery worldwide at around $20,500, with the charterer remaining unknown.

Atlantic
The Alpha Wisdom (81,305 2012) open Haldia 29 July fixed a trip to Singapore-Japan via EC South America, and the Mykonos (81,386 2013) open Hazira 10/11 August was reported to have been placed on subjects for similar business. ADM were said to have fixed the scrubber fitted Velos Libra (77,134 2014) in ballast towards EC South America, but no further details have emerged.

Asia
The Pacific market saw a steady flow of activity, with the scrubber fitted Shandong Xin Chang (82,161 2025) reportedly placed on subjects from Kobe on 6 August for a North Pacific round with grains in the high $19,000s, with the scrubber benefit for Owners, to Cofco. Elsewhere, the Emerald Putuo (85,611 2022) open Yeosu 7 August and the Seacon Antwerp (82,806 2024) open Nagoya 13 August were both reported fixed, though further details were unavailable. Yangze 12 (81,664 2019) was placed on subjects from Zhoushan on 9 August for an Indonesia to the Philippines trip with Norden, and Medi Eolie (81,845 2016) open Hong Kong on 10 August was placed on subjects for an Indonesia to India run. King Loong (77,430 2006) was placed on subjects by Tongli for an Indonesia to South China trip in the high $16,000's from Dung Quat on 10 August, while Samatan (77,154 2015) open Sual 12 August was placed on subjects for a similar Indonesia to South China trade with Norden. Additional Pacific business included the Yasa H. Mehmet (83,482 2011), open in Dangjin, which was placed on subjects for a Pacific round voyage at $16,000. The Tai Kinship (84,509 2021) was fixed from Hong Kong for 21/22 August delivery, with further details undisclosed. Meanwhile, Darya Preeti (81,981 2019) open Port Kelang 13/14 August was placed on subjects for a Richards Bay to Taiwan trip, and Melia (76,225 2005) fixed from Hong Kong on 6/7 August for an Indonesia to South China trip.
SUPRAMAX
A largely uneventful midweek with rates seemingly consolidating in the Atlantic, with the 11TC average only down $9 to settle at $20,381. The Continent has seen some Russian enquiry but is otherwise fairly quiet, the Mediterranean remains stronger in the East with the West still lacking the same demand and the South was said to have seen an increase in second half August stems which may help to steady rates there. In Asia the rates continue to soften with renewed concern of more upcoming weather delays affecting positions, with prompt vessels having to discount in order to cover now. A Dolphin 57k open Indonesia was rumoured to have fixed a trip Karachi with steel coils at $18,500, whilst in the Indian Ocean the Theologos S (63,787 2025) Kandla 8-10 August was placed on subjects for a trip via South Africa back to the Far East at $18,000 and the ND Thelxs (58,223 2012) open Krishnapatnam 7-10 August went on subjects for coastal trade at $16,500, but no Charterers were mentioned.
HANDYSIZE
Another lacklustre day for information reflecting the lack of fixing yesterday. Brokers suggest the market is generally flat despite the inactivity and this was reflected in todays Index with the US Gulf transatlantic trip the only real negative. The BHSI only dropped 2 to end 879 and the HS7TC average was down $43 to close at $15,821. On the Continent there were a few vessels fixed for scrap into the East Mediterranean, but details were hard to clarify, and there was little emanating from the Mediterranean. In Asia it was another slow day although one or two vessels have been placed on subjects apparently, and there was also some close trading on short period as we reach the middle of the week, which hopefully translates to a busier end to the week.
